short_answer: OddsShark is no longer a separate site. On 7 Nov 2026 oddsshark.com and its picks pages redirected to Covers, to a page headed "Odds Shark is now part of Covers." Covers' About page says it is part of the Genius Sports group and names CS Media Ltd as the operator. An archived copy from 1 Jun 2025 still showed OddsShark as its own site.

The picks are free. The NFL page on 7 Nov 2026 showed a computer projected score for each game, analyst picks with a rough post time such as "Pick made: yesterday," and betting trends. The page text says a table tracks the computer's results over the last 100 games at opening and closing lines, but no such table appeared on the page we opened, even fully loaded. We found no win and loss record for the computer or any analyst.

Covers earns from betting offers. The odds shown beside the picks link out through Covers redirect links to prediction market apps such as Kalshi and Novig, and the menus list dozens of promo code pages. Treat OddsShark picks as free content from an affiliate publisher, not a proven edge.
pricing_intro: Nothing on the OddsShark or Covers picks pages we opened on 7 Nov 2026 was for sale. Covers' About page says its core products are free, with no signup or subscription.

guarantee: There is nothing to guarantee because the picks are free. The real cost to a reader is the bets placed on them, and none of the pages we opened promised results.

claims_note: The page tells readers that the larger the projected score margin, the more confident the computer is. A projection is not a result. Without the results table the page describes, a reader cannot tell whether those projections have beaten the closing line.
Old OddsShark pick history is hard to find now that its pages redirect to Covers. We did not find an archive of past OddsShark computer picks with results.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing about OddsShark's picks. We found no outside monitor, contest or regulator record of its computer or analyst picks. Covers runs its own free contests, which we cover in our Covers expert picks review, but those grade Covers users, not the OddsShark computer.

What is the seller's own marketing: the NFL computer picks page says it tracks the last 100 games with record and profit at $100 a unit, at both opening and closing lines. That table was not on the page on 7 Nov 2026, so we cannot report a figure. Analyst picks showed names and rough times without a season record.
Legal history: our searches found no court or regulator action involving OddsShark. Covers' terms name CS Media Ltd, with a postal address in Post Falls, Idaho.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition neither the OddsShark computer nor any Covers analyst is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: free computer picks on spreads and totals have to clear the same bar as paid ones. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: OddsShark itself has almost no customer footprint we could find: its Trustpilot page has no reviews and it has no app of its own in the US App Store. Because its picks now live on Covers, we also read Covers reviews. Those mostly praise the free contests and research tools, and only one we found speaks to whether the picks win.

customers.text: We found no forum buyer of OddsShark picks, which are free on Covers. Covers members in 2024 called oddsshark.com a solid free stats site and liked its head to head database, while one wished it had day of the week splits. The only review we found that speaks to results, a 2026 Trustpilot review below, says tracked picks hit below 50 percent.
Trustpilot showed an OddsShark profile, claimed in Dec 2024 and listed in Canada, with 0 reviews.
SmartCustomer showed an unclaimed oddsshark.com page with 0 reviews.

A Covers reviewer on Trustpilot said he had tracked the site's computer picks and expert picks in baseball, basketball and football and found overall pick accuracy below 50%. He did not post his log, and we do not know whether the computer he tracked was the Odds Shark model now labeled on the page.
A short Covers review on Trustpilot praised the content and the free picks, with no mention of results.
A reviewer who said he had used Covers for 15 years credited it with teaching him about money management and pick strategy, and thanked handicappers who share opinions free. He gave no results.

Covers' Trustpilot page showed 4.7 from 264 reviews, 88% five star and 3% one star, with a note that the company had not invited reviews recently. The recent reviews mostly praise free contests and quick prize payouts rather than the picks.
The free Covers iPhone app, which its listing says offers expert picks, showed 4.7 out of 5 from 471 ratings. The top visible review, dated May 8 with no year shown, praised the clean layout.
Our searches found no Reddit, TheRX, SBR or Covers forum thread that evaluates OddsShark's computer picks record, and no OddsShark app in the US App Store.

conflicts: Covers, which now runs OddsShark, earns from betting operators. On the NFL picks page, the odds beside the computer picks link through Covers redirect links to Kalshi and Novig, and the site menus list promo code pages for sportsbooks, casinos, sweepstakes casinos and prediction markets.

Covers' DraftKings promo page says the offer applies when you sign up "through our exclusive link," labels it "Sponsored by DK" and a Covers and DraftKings partnership, and says affiliate links are disclosed. We saw no such disclosure next to the picks themselves.
OddsShark's "FinCertified" reviews rate the betting sites and casinos that the same network promotes.
Covers is part of Genius Sports, a sports data company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, according to the Covers About page.
strengths: Free, with no signup needed to see computer and analyst picks.
Computer picks cover every game on the board with projected scores, so you can compare them with your own numbers.
Covers names its operator, CS Media Ltd, and its parent group.
The page says results are tracked at both opening and closing lines, which is the right test if the table is published.
concerns: No results table or season record for the computer or the analysts was visible on 7 Nov 2026.
Prediction market and sportsbook links sit right beside the picks.
The move into Covers makes old OddsShark pick history hard to find.
Customer reviews are about Covers' contests and tools, not about whether these picks win.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes, as a real media brand: OddsShark is now part of Covers, which names CS Media Ltd as its operator and says it belongs to the Genius Sports group. That says nothing about whether its picks win, which we could not verify.
Nothing. The computer and analyst picks we saw on 7 Nov 2026 were free with no subscription; the site earns from sportsbook and prediction market offers instead.
Does OddsShark have a verified record?
No. We found no outside record, and the results table the computer picks page describes was not on the page when we checked. Watchdog has no graded record for it.

It is free, so you pay only with the bets you place, and you get projected scores and picks for every game. What is unproven is whether following them beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110, and the links beside them earn the site money when you sign up with a book or app.
